ideas.title: Climb anything: a grab that can slip
ideas.critique: This is the third time the same project has been pitched. What this round adds is a measured threshold and the lip curvature taken from the probe rays, so the slip on a rounded beam comes from geometry and not a tag. That answers the coin-flip worry, but only if the film is close and side-on enough to show a claw skidding along a lip; from far off, a fall looks like a missed animation. Load carried through a friction cone that can really fail, with speeds on the caption, is something the island has never done, and a wall you learn to read is a game people come back to.

ideas.title: Tippe top duel in a wooden bowl
ideas.critique: This is last round's tippe tops moved into a bowl, which gives the duel a reason for the clashes. A top inverting purely from friction torque can't be faked and is the kind of clip people share. Everything rests on the affine-body friction contact staying stable at high spin against a curved mesh; if it drifts or explodes, the flip never happens and you have tops falling over. The string pull is a thin skill, and once the pull is over the play is mostly watching.
